lsed

A software package (R and Python) for determining the benefit of using a statistical model in landscape decision making. Currently using minor extensions of decision curve analysis (DCA), geared towards species distribution models.

Overview

boop boop.

Installation

lsed is available only on github, with plans for submission to CRAN. It can be installed using remotes or devtools (or pak etc.):

install.packages('remotes')
remotes::install_github('sagesteppe/lsed')

Functions

The package splits into two toolkits: DCA Support (the prevalence-corrected evaluation of species-distribution predictions) and Prioritisation (building a RankIndex to prioritise sites for survey). Each function links to its reference page.

DCA Support

Function Purpose
reweight() Case weights that re-price an evaluation sample to a target prevalence
roc_auc() Prevalence-invariant ROC-AUC via the rank (Mann-Whitney) identity
ap_pointwise(), pr_curve_exact(), pr_auc() Exact average precision / PR curve / PR-AUC at a target prevalence
ap_binormal(), pr_curve_binormal(), ap_scalar_to_prev() Equal-variance binormal (summary-metric) route
nb_exact(), nb_exact_ci(), nb_binormal(), nb_binormal_band(), nb_treat_all() Decision-curve net benefit (per-point, CI, binormal, uncertainty band, treat-all)
cox_calibration(), recalibrate_to_prevalence(), clamp() Calibration of held-out predictions
point_residuals(), reduce_spatial_bias() Residual-kriging correction of spatially-structured prediction bias within the area of applicability

A vignette for these functions is located at Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes.

A vignette for these functions is located at Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes.

Prioritisation

Function Purpose
rank_download() One-call acquisition of every external input (GBIF records + OSM network)
gbif_records(), gbif_request(), gbif_retrieve() Pull target-group occurrence records from GBIF
osm_access(), osm_network_for() Fetch the OpenStreetMap road / trail network
survey_units() Delineate survey units from a continuous suitability raster
survey_surface(), survey_weights(), guess_record_type() Survey-intensity (bias) surface - the S term
geo_distance() Geographic distance to known populations - the Dg term
build_resistance(), cost_distance(), tobler_friction(), cluster_region_extents() Isotropic cost-distance engine - Dr / A terms
build_network(), contract_network(), accessibility(), complementarity() Network travel-time engine - A / C terms
osm_speeds Default per-highway travel speeds (km/h)
cluster_patches() Group nearby patches into spatial clusters
rank_index(), rank_calculate() Combine the terms into a priority score and ranking

A vignette for these functions is located at Prioritising sites for survey (RankIndex). Where you will, hopefully, happily see you only need to run two of them.
